assessment.title: Homework #8 · Basic amplifier configurations
assessment.topic: Module 8 · CS, discrete CS, emitter follower, common base
assessment.instructions: Show key steps, assumptions, and final answers with units. For each amplifier: find the DC bias, then the model parameters (g_m, r_o, r_e), draw the small-signal equivalent in the circuit workspace with capacitors shorted and DC supplies at AC ground, then compute the requested resistances and gains. Use V_T = 25 mV. Derivations are graded by hand; numerical results automatically. Practical task: predict first, build the schematic and breadboard yourself, check connections, test, and explain. Use Save progress in the homework toolbar, then reopen the downloaded JSON with Open saved homework. There is no homework file byte-size cap; available device memory and browser storage still apply. Keep a downloaded backup.

questions.title: 1) CS amplifier: R_in, A_vo, R_o, A_v, G_v and output swing
questions.promptHtml:
A common-source MOSFET amplifier is biased at ID = 0.25 mA, VOV = 0.25 V, with RD = 20 kΩ. The transistor has VA = 50 V. It is driven from Rsig = 100 kΩ, and RL = 20 kΩ is connected at the output.

Find (1) Rin, (2) the open-circuit voltage gain Avo, (3) Ro, (4) the loaded gain Av, and (5) the overall gain Gv = vo/vsig.

Then, if linearity limits the peak input sine amplitude to 10% of 2VOV, find the peak output sine amplitude.
hints: The gate draws no current, so R_in = ∞ and v_i = v_sig.

components.value: I_D = 0.25 mA, V_OV = 0.25 V (bias not shown)

questions.title: 2) Discrete CS amplifier: bias check and small-signal gains
questions.promptHtml:
The input is coupled to the gate through a very large capacitor; the source resistor is bypassed; the drain output is coupled to a 10 kΩ load. Given Rsig = 100 kΩ, gate-bias resistors 10 MΩ to +15 V and 5 MΩ to ground, RD = 7.5 kΩ, RS = 3 kΩ, RL = 10 kΩ, Vt = 1 V, kn = 2 mA/V2, VA = 100 V.

  1. Verify that the bias gives VGS = 2 V, ID = 1 mA, VD = +7.5 V.
  2. Find gm and ro.
  3. Draw the complete small-signal equivalent (all capacitors short) in the workspace.
  4. Find Rin, vgs/vsig, vo/vgs, and vo/vsig.
hints: V_G comes from the divider; V_S = I_D R_S; check both the square law and the loop.
With the source bypassed, the source is AC ground; R_G = 10 M∥5 M sits from gate to ground.
checklist: Bias: V_G, V_S, I_D (two ways), V_D, saturation check.

components.value: V_t = 1 V, k_n = 2 mA/V², V_A = 100 V

questions.promptHtml:

Rin = (β + 1)(re + Re)  and  vo/vi = Re/(Re + re).

Numerical check: β = 100, re = 25 Ω, Re = 1 kΩ.
hints: In the T model, r_e connects the internal emitter to the base; the collector source is αi_e.

questions.promptHtml: For the circuit shown (base grounded, emitter biased by a 0.5 mA current source, RC = 10 kΩ to +9 V, input from Rsig = 50 Ω through C1 = ∞ to the emitter, output through C2 = ∞ to RL = 10 kΩ), draw the complete small-signal equivalent using the T model with α = 0.99. Show the values of all components including the model parameters. Find Rin and the overall gain vo/vsig. Use VT = 25 mV.
hints: Looking into the emitter with the base grounded, R_in = r_e; the collector delivers αi_e into R_C∥R_L.
checklist: R_in, i_e = v_sig/(R_sig + r_e), v_o = αi_e(R_C∥R_L).

questions.title: 9) Circuit Studio · Measure a common-emitter amplifier on the Simulate bench
questions.promptHtml:
Start by connecting the components. The canvas contains the required components with their values, but no wires. Open Edit circuit, keep these components, and add the connections for the circuit described below. Check device pin names, source polarity and ground. Complete the schematic before using the solver or lenses. Test it on the canvas, then assemble the same circuit on the breadboard, check its wiring and compare measurements. Capture both your completed schematic and breadboard.

Circuit Studio problem · Simulate oscilloscope, Bode plot and I–V curves. Simulation tools are switched on for this question. Record each prediction before you use the tool that checks it.

A common-emitter amplifier: VCC = 12 V; RB1 = 100 kΩ, RB2 = 22 kΩ; RC = 4.7 kΩ; RE = 1 kΩ bypassed by Cb = 100 µF; vsig with Rsig = 1 kΩ through Cin; RL = 10 kΩ through Cout; β = 100, VT = 25.85 mV.

  1. Click Show values and record IC. Predict by hand from it: Rin = RB1 ∥ RB2 ∥ rπ and Gv = −gm(RC ∥ RL)·Rin/(Rin + Rsig).
  2. Open Simulate → Oscilloscope and Run with the 1 mV-peak, 1 kHz source. Record the gain CH2/CH1 and the phase.
  3. Raise the generator amplitude to 10 mV peak, Run again, and record the THD. Look at the output waveform: which half of the cycle is distorted, and why?
  4. Choose Bode plot, Run, and record the −3 dB (low) frequency. Change Cb to 1000 µF on the schematic and run the Bode plot again.
  5. Choose I–V curves, Run, and note the Q-point and the signal swing on the load line.
  6. Explain: why Gv is smaller than Av, why the low corner moved when Cb changed, and what limits the input amplitude.

Required build and test · Circuit Studio V2

Build the supplied common-emitter amplifier on schematic and breadboard. Verify transistor and electrolytic pin mapping and record its DC operating point. Set the generator to 1 mV peak, 1 kHz; connect CH1 to the generator before Rsig and CH2 to the loaded output to measure Gv. Increase the input to 10 mV peak and record distortion. Sweep frequency, identify the midband gain and low −3 dB corner, then compare Cb=100 µF and 1000 µF. Explain any difference between the hand model and the selected SPICE model.

  1. Record a prediction before running the solver. Match the stated component and model parameters; document any difference between the hand model and simulator.
  2. Use Edit circuit, then Build breadboard. Keep the supplied components on the canvas and connect them yourself. On the breadboard, place components and jumpers yourself; Guide me and X-Ray are allowed. Record any assistance used. Do not use Build for me as evidence of an independent build.
  3. Run the wiring check before power-on. Record the checker result, instrument terminals, source settings, measurements and units.
  4. Capture schematic, breadboard and test evidence with Capture lab evidence. For time traces, allow settling and state the measurement interval.
  5. Save progress, switch to another question and back, then reopen the downloaded progress file. Confirm that your answers, circuit, breadboard and instrument settings return.

The breadboard and measurements are virtual. Use simulated supplies only for this assignment.
hints: The bypass capacitor sees a small resistance (about r_e plus the source path), so it usually sets the low corner.
